en: The Third Collection (Tikanipāta), Chapter on the Inner Circle (Abbhantaravagga)
“Virtue alone, it is said, is beautiful;
virtue is supreme in the world.”
Behold the serpent of terrible venom;
though one is virtuous, he is not slain.
Therefore, I shall take up virtue as my refuge.
What is approved by the world is auspicious;
one who practices the conduct of the noble ones is called virtuous.
He is dear to his kinsmen and shines among his friends;
upon the dissolution of the body, he goes to a happy destination.
Thus ends the tenth Jātaka, the Sīlavīmaṁsaka-jātaka.
The fourth chapter, the Abbhantara-vagga, is concluded.
Its summary verse: The tree, the supreme bronze vessel, the tiger, the deer,
the jewels, the gem, the lotus-root, and the invocation.
And the excellent fish was also instructed by Maṇikuṇḍalaka with ten verses.
